approachQuestion.prompt: Answer many prefix-maximum requests. Given a read-only array of n signed measurements (1 <= n <= 100,000) and q valid indices (10,000 <= q <= 100,000), return the maximum among values[0..index] for each request. Example: values=[-4,2,0,7], indices=[0,2,3] returns [-4,2,7]. Choose a method that serves the whole batch efficiently.
constraints: All requests use the same unchanged array.
The result list is output and excluded from auxiliary-space accounting.

options.text: Make a running-maximum table from left to right, then read the stored maximum for each requested index.
options.feedback: Each prefix summary is computed once and directly reused by the batch.

options.text: For each requested index, scan from zero through that index and compute its maximum.
options.feedback: It is correct but repeats earlier comparisons; requests near the end make it revisit comparisons already made for earlier prefixes.

options.text: Sort all measurements and use the largest value as every answer.
options.feedback: It uses the maximum of the entire array instead of the requested prefix. For values=[-4,2,0] and index=0, it returns 2 instead of -4.

options.text: Build running minimums and return the stored value for each requested index.
options.feedback: This answers a different question. For values=[-4,2,0] and index=2, it returns -4 instead of 2.

feedback.reason: Each requested prefix has a summary that can be extended from the preceding one.
details: Set the first prefix maximum to the first measurement. At every later index, store the larger of the current value and the previous prefix maximum. Answer each request by reading the entry at its index.

For [-4,2,0,7], the stored maxima are [-4,2,2,7]. Initialize from the first measurement, not zero: an all-negative prefix still has a negative maximum. This answers prefixes; subtracting two maxima cannot produce an arbitrary interval maximum.
“Make a running-maximum table from left to right, then read the stored maximum for each requested index.”: Each prefix summary is computed once and directly reused by the batch.

“For each requested index, scan from zero through that index and compute its maximum.”: It is correct but repeats earlier comparisons; requests near the end make it revisit comparisons already made for earlier prefixes.

“Sort all measurements and use the largest value as every answer.”: It uses the maximum of the entire array instead of the requested prefix. For values=[-4,2,0] and index=0, it returns 2 instead of -4.
“Build running minimums and return the stored value for each requested index.”: This answers a different question. For values=[-4,2,0] and index=2, it returns -4 instead of 2.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for prefix-maximum-table. The returned answers are output and excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: The table stores one maximum per input position.
Each query reads one table entry.

options.text: O(n + q) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build n running maxima and answer q indexed requests.
details: The recurrence max(previousMaximum,currentValue) fills n stored maxima once. q indexed reads add O(q), giving O(n+q) time. The n-entry table is auxiliary, not returned output. Recomputing each requested maximum from the start would instead repeat prefix work.
